1	# Cloudflare Radar 2024 Year in Review
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	
     5	URL: https://radar.cloudflare.com/year-in-review/2024
     6	
     7	The Cloudflare Radar 2024 Year in Review provides a comprehensive view of Internet patterns and trends observed through Cloudflare's global network during 2024. The report covers traffic growth, popular services, technology adoption, connectivity disruptions, security threats, and email security trends. Data is derived from Cloudflare's position as a provider protecting and accelerating websites and applications for millions of customers worldwide.
     8	
     9	## Internet Traffic Growth and Popular Services
    10	
    11	Global Internet traffic grew by 17% in 2024, continuing the upward trend driven by increasing reliance on the Internet for communication, commerce, entertainment, and transportation. The trend line starts mid-January to normalize for post-holiday activity.
    12	
    13	Google maintained its position as the most popular Internet service overall, topping the rankings for the second consecutive year. Generative AI continued its rapid rise throughout 2024, while the Metaverse receded into the background. The ranking methodology is based on aggregate data from Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver.
    14	
    15	| Rank | Service   |
    16	|------|-----------|
    17	| #1   | Google    |
    18	| #2   | Facebook  |
    19	| #3   | Apple     |
    20	| #4   | TikTok    |
    21	| #5   | AWS       |
    22	| #6   | Microsoft |
    23	| #7   | Instagram |
    24	| #8   | YouTube   |
    25	| #9   | Amazon    |
    26	| #10  | WhatsApp  |
    27	
    28	![Top 10 most popular Internet services worldwide](./assets/top-10-internet-services.jpg)
    29	
    30	SpaceX Starlink traffic saw dramatic 3.3x growth during 2024, continuing to bring satellite Internet connectivity to previously underserved locations. Starlink is not yet available globally; the trend line is scaled relative to peak observed request volume.
    31	
    32	![Normalized Starlink traffic worldwide showing 3.3x growth in 2024](./assets/starlink-traffic-growth-2024.jpg)
    33	
    34	## Technology Adoption and Usage Patterns
    35	
    36	Several key adoption metrics emerged from the 2024 data:
    37	
    38	- **Mobile OS**: 33% of traffic came from iOS devices. Apple iOS and Google Android remain the dominant mobile operating systems, with peak Android traffic share exceeding 95% in some regions and peak iOS reaching around 66%.
    39	- **HTTP/3**: 21% of traffic uses HTTP/3, the most recent version of the protocol that runs on top of QUIC, providing faster connections, packet-loss mitigation, and encryption by default.
    40	- **Search Engines**: Google dominates with 89% of search engine referral traffic, followed by Yandex (3.1%), Baidu (2.7%), Bing (2.6%), DuckDuckGo (0.95%), and other engines (2.2%).
    41	- **Browsers**: Chrome remains the most popular browser globally.
    42	- **API Client Languages**: Go is the most popular API client language with approximately 12% of automated API requests, followed by Node.js, Python (9.6%), Java (7.4%), and .NET (3.6%).
    43	
    44	Post-quantum encryption saw a dramatic surge in adoption during 2024. Starting at around 2% of TLS 1.3 traffic in early 2024, adoption jumped sharply following Google Chrome 124 enabling post-quantum key agreement by default on April 17, rapidly climbing to approximately 12-13%. Mozilla Firefox has also started rolling out post-quantum by default, and Apple Safari began initial testing.
    45	
    46	![Post-quantum encrypted traffic worldwide showing rapid adoption after Chrome 124 release](./assets/post-quantum-encryption-adoption.jpg)
    47	
    48	## Internet Connectivity and Disruptions
    49	
    50	Cloudflare observed 225 major Internet disruptions globally in 2024. These outages result from a variety of causes, and the Cloudflare Radar Outage Center tracks their scope and duration using Cloudflare traffic data.
    51	
    52	The leading causes of Internet disruptions were:
    53	
    54	| Cause                | Count |
    55	|----------------------|-------|
    56	| Government Directed  | 116+  |
    57	| Cable Cut            | 41    |
    58	| Unknown              | 16    |
    59	| Power Outage         | 16    |
    60	| Technical Problem    | 9     |
    61	| Military Action      | 9     |
    62	| Weather              | 8     |
    63	| Maintenance          | 4     |
    64	| Cyber Attack         | 4     |
    65	| Natural Disaster     | 1     |
    66	| Fire                 | 1     |
    67	
    68	![Causes of major Internet disruptions observed in 2024](./assets/internet-disruption-causes.jpg)
    69	
    70	IPv6 adoption reached 28% of dual-stack traffic during 2024. Spain recorded the highest download speed among all countries measured.
    71	
    72	41% of global traffic came from mobile devices, reflecting the continued importance of mobile connectivity worldwide.
    73	
    74	## Security Landscape
    75	
    76	Cloudflare mitigated 6.5% of all traffic it processed, indicating the scale of ongoing threats. The Gambling and Games sector was the most attacked industry category. Notably, 68% of global bot traffic originated from just the top 10 countries.
    77	
    78	The Log4j vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228), first disclosed in December 2021, continues to be actively targeted by attackers more than two years later, underscoring the persistent nature of widely known vulnerabilities.
    79	
    80	RPKI (Resource Public Key Infrastructure) valid routes increased by 6.4%, an important step toward improved Internet routing security.
    81	
    82	## Email Security Threats
    83	
    84	Cloudflare's email security analysis revealed that 4.3% of emails processed were malicious. Among those malicious emails, 43% contained a deceptive link designed to trick recipients. The top-level domain .bar originated the largest share of malicious and spam email observed during the year.
    85	
    86	## Key Findings
    87	
    88	- Global Internet traffic grew 17% year-over-year, with Starlink traffic surging 3.3x as satellite connectivity expanded to underserved regions.
    89	- Post-quantum encryption adoption leapt from approximately 2% to 13% of TLS 1.3 traffic following Chrome 124's default enablement in April 2024.
    90	- Government-directed shutdowns remained the leading cause of the 225 major Internet disruptions observed, followed by cable cuts (41 incidents) and power outages (16).
    91	- Security threats remained pervasive: 6.5% of all traffic was mitigated, Gambling/Games was the most targeted sector, and Log4j exploitation persists years after disclosure.
    92	- Go surpassed other languages to become the most popular API client language, capturing roughly 12% of automated API traffic.

     6	description: "Create, inspect, and edit Microsoft PowerPoint presentations and PPTX decks with reliable layouts, templates, placeholders, notes, charts, and visual QA. Use when (1) the task is about PowerPoint or `.pptx`; (2) layouts, placeholders, notes, charts, comments, or template fidelity matter; (3) the deck must render cleanly after edits."
     7	changelog: Rebalanced the skill toward template inventory, layout mapping, and higher-signal QA after a stricter external audit.

     9	---
    10	
    11	## When to Use
    12	
    13	Use when the main artifact is a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation or `.pptx` deck, especially when layouts, templates, placeholders, notes, comments, charts, extraction, editing, or final visual quality matter.
    14	
    15	## Core Rules
    16	
    17	### 1. Choose the workflow before touching the deck
    18	
    19	- Reading text, editing an existing deck, rebuilding from a template, and creating from scratch are different jobs with different failure modes.
    20	- For text extraction or inspection, read the deck before editing it.
    21	- Text extraction plus thumbnail-style visual inspection is safer than editing from shape assumptions alone.
    22	- For template-driven work, inventory the deck before replacing content.
    23	- For deep edits, remember a `.pptx` file is OOXML with separate parts for slides, layouts, masters, media, notes, and comments.
    24	- If a template exists, template fidelity beats generic slide-design instincts.
    25	- Reusing or duplicating a good existing slide is often safer than rebuilding it and hoping the theme still matches.
    26	
    27	### 2. Inventory the deck before replacing content
    28	
    29	- Count the reusable layouts, real placeholders, notes, comments, media, and recurring typography or color patterns first.
    30	- Placeholder indexes and layout indexes are not portable assumptions.
    31	- Inspect the actual slide or template before targeting title, body, chart, or image shapes.
    32	- Speaker notes, comments, and linked assets can live outside the visible slide surface.
    33	- A missing or wrong placeholder target can silently land content in the wrong box or wrong layer.
    34	- Master and layout settings can override local slide edits, so the visible problem is not always on the slide you are editing.
    35	
    36	### 3. Match content to the actual placeholders
    37	
    38	- Count the actual content pieces before choosing a layout.
    39	- Pick layouts based on the real number of ideas, columns, images, or charts the slide needs.
    40	- Do not force two ideas into a three-column slide or cram dense text under a chart.
    41	- Category counts and data series lengths must match or charts will break in ugly ways.
    42	- Explicit sizing beats wishful thinking: text boxes, images, and charts need real space, not "it should fit".
    43	- Do not choose a layout with more placeholders than the content can meaningfully fill.
    44	- Quote layouts are for real quotes, and image-led layouts are for slides that actually have images.
    45	- For chart-, table-, or image-heavy slides, full-slide or two-column layouts are usually safer than stacking dense text above the visual.
    46	
    47	### 4. Preserve the deck's visual language
    48	
    49	- Theme, master, and layout files usually decide fonts, colors, and hierarchy more than any one slide does.
    50	- Start from the deck's actual theme, fonts, spacing, and aspect ratio instead of improvising a new style.
    51	- Reuse the deck's own alignment and spacing system instead of inventing a second visual language.
    52	- Use common fonts for portability and strong contrast for readability.
    53	- Preserve the template's visual logic first; originality matters less than not breaking the deck's existing language.
    54	- Combining slides from multiple sources requires normalizing themes, masters, and alignment afterward.
    55	
    56	### 5. Run content QA and visual QA separately
    57	
    58	- Text overflow, bad alignment, clipped shapes, weak contrast, and placeholder leftovers are normal first-pass failures.
    59	- Run both content QA and visual QA; missing text and broken layout are different failure classes.
    60	- Render or inspect the actual deck output before delivery when layout matters.
    61	- Search for leftover template junk, sample labels, and placeholder text before calling the deck finished.
    62	- Check notes, comments, labels, legends, and chart/table semantics separately from the visual pass.
    63	- A deck can pass text extraction and still fail on overlap, clipping, wrong theme inheritance, or broken notes.
    64	- Thumbnail grids and rendered slides usually reveal layout bugs faster than code or text inspection.
    65	- Assume the first render is wrong and do at least one fix-and-verify cycle before calling the deck finished.
    66	- Re-check affected slides after each fix because one spacing change often creates another issue.
    67	
    68	### 6. Keep decks portable and review-safe
    69	
    70	- Template masters can override direct edits in surprising ways.
    71	- Complex effects may degrade across PowerPoint, LibreOffice, and conversion pipelines, so keep important content robust without them.
    72	- Image sizing, font substitution, and placeholder mismatch are common reasons a deck looks good in code and bad on screen.
    73	- Notes, comments, linked media, and merged decks can stay broken even when the visible slide looks fine.
    74	
    75	## Common Traps
    76	
    77	- Placeholder text and sample charts often survive template reuse if not explicitly replaced.
    78	- Directly editing one slide can fail if the real issue lives in the master or layout.
    79	- Charts, icons, and text boxes need enough space; near-collisions are usually visible only after rendering.
    80	- Layout indexes vary by template, so built-in assumptions from one deck often break in another.
    81	- A missing placeholder or wrong shape target can silently put content in the wrong place.
    82	- Counting the text ideas after choosing the layout usually leads to empty placeholders, weak hierarchy, or leftover template junk.
    83	- Font substitution can move line breaks and wreck careful spacing.
    84	- Speaker notes, comments, and linked media can stay broken even when the visible slide looks fine.
    85	- A deck can pass text inspection and still fail visually because of overlap, contrast, or edge clipping.
    86	- Editing from one slide alone can miss the real source of truth in the theme, master, or layout definitions.
    87	- Choosing a quote, comparison, or multi-column layout without matching content usually makes the deck look templated rather than intentional.
    88	- Combining or duplicating slides without checking masters and themes can create subtle inconsistency slide by slide.
    89	- Aspect-ratio mismatches like `16:9` versus `4:3` can shift every placement decision even when each slide looks locally reasonable.
    90	
    91	## Related Skills
    92	Install with `clawhub install <slug>` if user confirms:
    93	- `documents` — Document workflows that often feed presentation content.
    94	- `design` — Visual direction and layout decisions.
    95	- `brief` — Concise business messaging for slide narratives.
    96	
    97	## Feedback
    98	
    99	- If useful: `clawhub star powerpoint-pptx`
   100	- Stay updated: `clawhub sync`

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RgbColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.oxml.ns import nsmap
from pptx.oxml import parse_xml
import os

# Create presentation 16:9
prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

# Color scheme - dark navy consistent with Cloudflare Radar aesthetic
NAVY_BG = RgbColor(0x0A, 0x0E, 0x1A)        # Very dark navy background
DARK_NAVY = RgbColor(0x0F, 0x17, 0x2A)      # Slightly lighter navy for cards
ACCENT_ORANGE = RgbColor(0xF9, 0x5C, 0x1A)  # Cloudflare orange
ACCENT_BLUE = RgbColor(0x40, 0x8C, 0xFF)    # Bright blue accent
WHITE = RgbColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
LIGHT_GRAY = RgbColor(0xB0, 0xB8, 0xC8)
MEDIUM_GRAY = RgbColor(0x6B, 0x75, 0x85)
DARK_GRAY = RgbColor(0x2A, 0x35, 0x4A)

def add_background(slide, color=NAVY_BG):
    """Add solid background color to slide"""
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size, font_color=WHITE, bold=False, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Segoe UI"):
    """Add a text box with specified formatting"""
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = font_size
    p.font.color.rgb = font_color
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return txBox

def add_card(slide, left, top, width, height, color=DARK_NAVY):
    """Add a rounded rectangle card"""
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape

def add_accent_bar(slide, left, top, width, height, color=ACCENT_ORANGE):
    """Add an accent bar"""
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape

# ============================================================
# SLIDE 1: Title Slide
# ============================================================
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # Blank
slide1 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_background(slide1)

# Accent bar at top
add_accent_bar(slide1, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.08), ACCENT_ORANGE)

# Main title
add_textbox(slide1, Inches(1), Inches(2.4), Inches(11.333), Inches(1.2),
            "Cloudflare Radar 2024 Year in Review",
            Pt(48), WHITE, bold=True, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# Subtitle
add_textbox(slide1, Inches(1), Inches(3.6), Inches(11.333), Inches(0.8),
            "A data-driven analysis of global Internet traffic, adoption trends, connectivity disruptions, and security threats",
            Pt(20), LIGHT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# Date / scope line
add_textbox(slide1, Inches(1), Inches(4.5), Inches(11.333), Inches(0.5),
            "Observed through Cloudflare's global network | 2024",
            Pt(14), MEDIUM_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# Bottom accent bar
add_accent_bar(slide1, Inches(0), Inches(7.42), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.08), ACCENT_ORANGE)

# ============================================================
# SLIDE 2: 17% Global Traffic Growth and Starlink's 3.3x Surge
# ============================================================
slide2 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_background(slide2)
add_accent_bar(slide2, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.06), ACCENT_ORANGE)

# Title
add_textbox(slide2, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.3), Inches(12.333), Inches(0.7),
            "17% Global Traffic Growth and Starlink's 3.3x Surge",
            Pt(32), WHITE, bold=True)

# Left card - 17% growth
add_card(slide2, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.2), Inches(5.8), Inches(2.6), DARK_NAVY)
add_textbox(slide2, Inches(0.7), Inches(1.35), Inches(5.4), Inches(0.6),
            "Global Internet Traffic Growth", Pt(18), LIGHT_GRAY, bold=True)
add_textbox(slide2, Inches(0.7), Inches(1.9), Inches(5.4), Inches(0.9),
            "17%", Pt(56), ACCENT_ORANGE, bold=True)
add_textbox(slide2, Inches(0.7), Inches(2.7), Inches(5.4), Inches(1.0),
            "Year-over-year increase in 2024, continuing the upward trend driven by increasing reliance on the Internet for communication, commerce, entertainment, and transportation.",
            Pt(13), LIGHT_GRAY)

# Right card - Starlink 3.3x
add_card(slide2, Inches(6.9), Inches(1.2), Inches(5.8), Inches(2.6), DARK_NAVY)
add_textbox(slide2, Inches(7.1), Inches(1.35), Inches(5.4), Inches(0.6),
            "SpaceX Starlink Traffic Surge", Pt(18), LIGHT_GRAY, bold=True)
add_textbox(slide2, Inches(7.1), Inches(1.9), Inches(5.4), Inches(0.9),
            "3.3x", Pt(56), ACCENT_BLUE, bold=True)
add_textbox(slide2, Inches(7.1), Inches(2.7), Inches(5.4), Inches(1.0),
            "Dramatic growth during 2024, continuing to bring satellite Internet connectivity to previously underserved locations. Trend scaled relative to peak observed request volume.",
            Pt(13), LIGHT_GRAY)

# Bottom image - Starlink chart
if os.path.exists("/app/benchmark/assets/starlink-traffic-growth-2024.jpg"):
    slide2.shapes.add_picture("/app/benchmark/assets/starlink-traffic-growth-2024.jpg",
                               Inches(0.5), Inches(4.1), Inches(12.333), Inches(3.0))

add_accent_bar(slide2, Inches(0), Inches(7.44), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.06), ACCENT_ORANGE)

# ============================================================
# SLIDE 3: Google Leads Top 10 Services as Generative AI Rises
# ============================================================
slide3 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_background(slide3)
add_accent_bar(slide3, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.06), ACCENT_ORANGE)

# Title
add_textbox(slide3, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.3), Inches(12.333), Inches(0.7),
            "Google Leads Top 10 Services as Generative AI Rises",
            Pt(32), WHITE, bold=True)

# Left: Top 10 table card
add_card(slide3, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.1), Inches(5.8), Inches(5.8), DARK_NAVY)
add_textbox(slide3, Inches(0.7), Inches(1.2), Inches(5.4), Inches(0.4),
            "Top 10 Most Popular Internet Services", Pt(16), WHITE, bold=True)

# Table
rows = 11
cols = 2
table_left = Inches(0.7)
table_top = Inches(1.7)
table_width = Inches(5.4)
table_height = Inches(5.0)
table = slide3.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, table_left, table_top, table_width, table_height).table

# Set column widths
table.columns[0].width = Inches(1.0)
table.columns[1].width = Inches(4.4)

services = [
    ("Rank", "Service"),
    ("#1", "Google"),
    ("#2", "Facebook"),
    ("#3", "Apple"),
    ("#4", "TikTok"),
    ("#5", "AWS"),
    ("#6", "Microsoft"),
    ("#7", "Instagram"),
    ("#8", "YouTube"),
    ("#9", "Amazon"),
    ("#10", "WhatsApp"),
]

for i, (rank, svc) in enumerate(services):
    cell0 = table.cell(i, 0)
    cell1 = table.cell(i, 1)
    cell0.text = rank
    cell1.text = svc
    for cell in (cell0, cell1):
        for paragraph in cell.text_frame.paragraphs:
            paragraph.font.size = Pt(13)
            paragraph.font.name = "Segoe UI"
            if i == 0:
                paragraph.font.bold = True
                paragraph.font.color.rgb = WHITE
            else:
                paragraph.font.color.rgb = LIGHT_GRAY
    cell0.fill.solid()
    cell0.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK_GRAY if i == 0 else DARK_NAVY
    cell1.fill.solid()
    cell1.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK_GRAY if i == 0 else DARK_NAVY

# Right: Generative AI insight + image
add_card(slide3, Inches(6.9), Inches(1.1), Inches(5.8), Inches(2.0), DARK_NAVY)
add_textbox(slide3, Inches(7.1), Inches(1.2), Inches(5.4), Inches(0.4),
            "Generative AI on the Rise", Pt(16), WHITE, bold=True)
add_textbox(slide3, Inches(7.1), Inches(1.65), Inches(5.4), Inches(1.3),
            "Generative AI continued its rapid rise throughout 2024, while the Metaverse receded into the background. Google maintained its #1 position for the second consecutive year. Rankings based on aggregate data from Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver.",
            Pt(12), LIGHT_GRAY)
